Run and configure the clients

Desktop client

Download a package for your platform from Get the game on the home page and extract the complete archive. Keep the executable with its bundled libraries and music directory. From an extracted native package, run bin/lineclash on macOS or Linux, or bin/lineclash.exe on Windows. From a source build, run ./clients/gui/lineclash (clients/gui/lineclash.exe on Windows). Build instructions are on Source.

In the main menu, Public servers loads the official directory from https://lineclash.example.org/api/. Local network searches nearby servers directly over UDP and uses their LAN address. Saved servers contains your locally stored endpoints and offers Add, Edit and Remove controls. Use Saved servers for private hosts and ports. You can save or edit an endpoint while it is offline; account credentials are optional until connecting. Public entries cannot be renamed or removed from the directory by a client. Favourite a public endpoint to keep a local copy. The default game port is 31457. For a server on this computer, use localhost. Enter your nickname and password, then connect. New names register when the server allows registration; existing names require their original password. Accounts belong to each server.

Select a room, choose a team if wanted, and ready up. The room host controls rules, bots and starting the round. Leave the room to return to the lobby; disconnect before choosing another server. Use Quit in the main menu or close the window to stop the desktop client.

Desktop preferences and saved servers

Use Settings → Controls to change gameplay bindings and display preferences. Music and SFX controls set their respective volume and enabled state. The menu plays the title theme; during a round, Music Player provides track selection, pause, seek and shuffle. Track attribution is available in the player, About and the website Credits page.

Preferences and saved server entries are stored locally:

Platform Preferences Saved servers
macOS / Linux ~/.lineclash_settings ~/.lineclash_servers
Windows %APPDATA%\LineClash\settings %APPDATA%\LineClash\servers

Close the client before backing up or changing these files. Saved authentication hashes can grant account access: keep them private. To reset preferences, close the game and rename the settings file; the next launch uses defaults. Keep the original file if you want to restore your bindings later.

Terminal client — macOS and Linux

The terminal client is available from a source build on macOS and Linux. It is not part of the native Windows client target. Open a terminal and run:

./clients/cli/lineclash-cli localhost 31457

For saved connections, see the options supported by your installed version:

./clients/cli/lineclash-cli --help
./clients/cli/lineclash-cli --list
./clients/cli/lineclash-cli --connect YOUR_SAVED_ALIAS

--cfg PATH selects a separate credentials file. The help output shows its default location. Adding profiles with --password or supplying a password as a positional argument can expose it through shell history and process listings. Protect saved credentials as carefully as passwords.

Follow the contextual footer for each screen. In a room, R readies, S starts as host, T edits the team, E/M/H adds an easy/medium/hard bot, X removes a bot and Q leaves. During play, arrows move, Up/Z rotate, Down soft-drops, Space hard-drops, C holds and Tab opens chat. Number keys target specials. Use the contextual quit/leave command to exit.

The terminal client uses the legacy board-reporting protocol; rounds involving it are casual. The desktop client supports server-processed inputs for eligible ranked rounds.

Connection problems

Check the server host and game port first; the HTTP status port is not a game endpoint. Unreachable usually requires checking that the server is running, its address is correct and the game port is reachable through the firewall. Wrong credentials requires the correct password for that server. Server full requires a free slot, while Protocol mismatch requires a compatible client/server version. Access-denied or banned accounts require assistance from that server's administrator.

During an active-game connection loss, automatic reconnect freezes local play while the server reserves your slot. Escape cancels recovery in the GUI; Q/Escape cancels in the terminal. An expired reservation, completed round or server restart requires reconnecting normally. See game basics.

Controls and accessibility

Default desktop controls

Action Key
Move left / right Left / Right, or A / D
Rotate clockwise Up, or W
Rotate counterclockwise Z
Soft drop Down, or S
Hard drop Space
Hold C or Shift
Chat Tab
Ready in room R
Pause F5, subject to room permissions
Target a player / use a special 1–8 using the displayed player IDs

Change gameplay bindings in Settings → Controls. The room host starts rounds from the room controls. Spectators can use arrows to switch the watched player.

Make the game easier to read

Press F2 to open or close Settings. Its Display tab includes window size, piece patterns and high contrast; Audio contains music and effects preferences. These preferences are saved locally.

  • F6 cycles 75%, 100%, 125% and 150% window sizes, bounded by the available display. You can also resize the window.
  • F7 toggles distinct piece markers, so piece types can be identified without relying on color alone.
  • F4 toggles higher-contrast text.

F2, F4, F6 and F7 are reserved for those options and cannot be assigned to gameplay actions. Website controls also have visible keyboard-focus outlines, and the background respects reduced-motion preferences.

Xbox and PlayStation controllers

The desktop client uses SDL's controller mappings for supported Xbox and PlayStation pads over USB or Bluetooth. Enable Controller input in Settings → Display. Support depends on the operating system, connection and SDL mapping for the specific model. The terminal client does not use controllers.

Xbox / PlayStation In-game action
D-pad left/right or left stick Move
D-pad down or left stick down Soft drop
A / Cross Rotate clockwise
B / Circle Rotate counterclockwise
X / Square or LB / L1 Hold
Y / Triangle or D-pad up Hard drop
Start / Options Pause, subject to room permissions

Movement repeats while held. A stick dead zone prevents slight drift from moving pieces. Pads may connect or disconnect while the game runs. Input is ignored when the game loses focus or a dialog is open. Controllers follow the configured gameplay key bindings; keyboard and mouse remain available for menus, chat and special targeting. Full controller-only menu navigation is not provided.
